title: Assigning Entitlements to Users and User Groups

blocks.text: You can assign an individual user or user group to a Zscaler service. You can assign users to perform administrative tasks via administrative entitlements or assign them as end users via service entitlements. To view the list of entitlements for a specific user, see Viewing Entitlements Assigned to Users.
Before assigning users or user groups, you must first add these users and groups to Authentication Service.

If your organization uses Unified Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), administrator roles for Authentication Service are managed on a different Role Management page. To learn more, see About Role Management. Unified RBAC is a feature in limited availability. To access Unified RBAC, contact your Zscaler Account team.
To assign users to a Zscaler service for performing administrative tasks:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Administration > Role Management > Administrative Entitlements.
Click the required Zscaler service's name.
See image.
Assign users via one of these methods:
Assign users individually
On the Users tab, click Assign Users.
See image.
The Assign Users wizard appears.
In the Assign Users wizard:
On the Select Users & Roles page, select the users that must be assigned to the Zscaler service.

From the Role column, select the role that must be assigned to each user. The drop-down menu includes a list of roles configured in the Zscaler Admin Console. To learn more, see Configuring Administrator Roles.
See image.
For tenants that are not enabled with Unified RBAC, admins cannot create, modify or delete the entitlement and role assigned to them in Authentication Service Administrative entitlement.
(Optional) To apply the same role for all groups, enable Set same role for all selected users, and select the specific role from the drop-down menu.
See image.
The Microtenant column is visible only for the Private Access (ZPA) service. You can assign and manage Microtenants for other admins if you have the following administrative entitlement permissions:

table: Assign, edit, or delete any Microtenant to other admins
Restricted Full and assigned a Default Microtenant in Private Access
Assign, edit, or delete any Microtenant to other admins
Restricted Full and assigned a Microtenant but not Default Microtenant
Assign, edit, or delete assigned Microtenant to other admins

blocks.item: If no Microtenant is configured in Private Access, select Default in the Microtenant column.
Click Next.
On the Summary page, review the assignment details and click Assign.
See image.
The selected users are assigned to the Zscaler service with administrative privileges.
Assign users via user groups

If a user is assigned to a service's admin role individually, but they are also a part of a user group with a different admin role, then the role assigned to the individual user takes precedence over the user group role.
On the User Groups tab, click Assign Groups.
See image.
The Assign Groups wizard appears.
In the Assign Groups wizard:
On the Select Groups & Roles page, select the user groups that must be assigned to the Zscaler service.

From the Role column, select the role that must be assigned to each user group. The drop-down menu includes a list of roles configured in the Zscaler Admin Console. To learn more, see Configuring Administrator Roles.
See image.
(Optional) To apply the same role for all groups, enable Set same role for all selected groups, and select the specific role from the drop-down menu.
See image.

The Microtenant column is visible only for the Private Access (ZPA) service. Select the Microtenant for the admins within the Private Access service in the Zscaler Admin Console. To learn more, see About Microtenants.
If no Microtenant is configured in the Private Access, you must select Default in the Microtenant column.
Click Next.
On the Summary page, review the assignment details and click Assign.
See image.
The selected user groups are assigned to the Zscaler service with administrative privileges for all users in the groups.

blocks.text: To assign users to a Zscaler service:

blocks.item: Go to Administration > Subscription > End User Entitlements.
Click the required Zscaler service's name.
See image.
Assign users via one of these methods:
Assign users individually
On the Users tab, click Assign Users.
See image.
The Assign Users wizard appears.
In the Assign Users wizard:
On the Select Users page, select the users that must be assigned to the Zscaler service.
See image.
Click Next.
On the Summary page, review the assignment details and click Assign.
See image.
The selected users are assigned to the Zscaler service as end users.
Assign users via user groups
On the User Groups tab, click Assign Groups.
See image.
The Assign Groups wizard appears.
In the Assign Groups wizard:
On the Select Groups page, select the user groups that must be assigned to the Zscaler service.
See image.
Click Next.
On the Summary page, review the assignment details and click Assign.
See image.
The selected user groups are assigned to the Zscaler service.
